title: Coding and testing
subtitle: Testing cannot prove a program correct — but well-chosen tests find most of the bugs, cheaply.

sections.title: Coding practice
sections.body: Follow a coding standard: meaningful names, small functions, comments that say why, consistent layout, no duplicated logic. Code review catches defects and spreads knowledge. Refactoring improves structure without changing behaviour — safely, only with tests.

sections.title: Levels of testing
sections.body: Unit tests check one function; integration tests check modules together; system tests check the whole against requirements; acceptance tests are run by the customer. The test pyramid says: many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests, very few slow end-to-end tests.

questions.prompt: Which tests should be most numerous?

figures.caption: Figure 6.2.1 — test pyramid
figures.note: The wider the layer, the more tests.
figures.script:
diagram("direction: down
[Few: end-to-end / acceptance] as e
[Some: integration] as i
[Many: unit] as u
e -> i
i -> u");

sections.title: Black-box techniques
sections.body: Equivalence partitioning: split inputs into classes that should behave alike and test one of each. Boundary value analysis: bugs cluster at edges, so test min, min+1, max−1, max and just outside. A field accepting ages 18–60 has partitions <18, 18–60, >60 and boundaries 17, 18, 19, 59, 60, 61.

worked.why: Valid range 18–60. Boundary tests (two-value form): below, on, above each end.

questions.prompt: For inputs 1–100, which set is a boundary test?

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: Just outside and on both edges.

problems.prompt: A quantity field accepts 1–10. List boundary values.

sections.title: White-box and cyclomatic complexity
sections.body: Coverage measures how much code the tests execute: statement, branch, path. Cyclomatic complexity V(G) = E − N + 2 (or decisions + 1) counts independent paths — the minimum number of test cases for basis-path coverage. V(G) above about 10 marks code that should be split.

sections.title: Test-driven development
sections.body: Write a failing test (red), write just enough code to pass (green), then clean up (refactor), and repeat. The tests document behaviour and let you change code fearlessly.

questions.prompt: In TDD the first step is…

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: It proves the test can fail.

sections.title: Debugging and reliability
sections.body: Reproduce, isolate (bisect the input or the history), find the cause, fix, add a regression test. Reliability is measured by MTBF; availability = MTBF/(MTBF + MTTR).
